objective.text: Inject a service into rules through the container instead of reading global state.

difficulty.rationale: Resolve a method dependency before constructing data-dependent rules.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

files.source:
<?php

use Illuminate\Foundation\Http\FormRequest;

class PlanLimits
{
    public int $members = 2;
}

class InviteRequest extends FormRequest
{
    public function authorize(): bool
    {
        return true;
    }

    public function rules(PlanLimits $limits): array
    {
        return ['members' => ['required', 'array', 'max:'.$limits->members]];
    }
}

stem: No custom binding overrides PlanLimits. Three members are submitted. Which outcome follows when Laravel validates this request?

options.text: The maximum is interpreted as two bytes of JSON.
options.rationale: For an array-valued field, max constrains its item count rather than serialized byte length.
options.misconception: For an array-valued field, max constrains its item count rather than serialized byte length.

options.text: A missing PlanLimits argument error occurs before validation.
options.rationale: Laravel supplies this concrete dependency through the container; no manual argument is required.
options.misconception: Laravel supplies this concrete dependency through the container; no manual argument is required.

options.text: Validation fails because rules receives PlanLimits and limits the array to two entries.
options.rationale: Laravel calls the rules method through the container, resolves PlanLimits, and applies max:2 to the members array.

options.text: Validation passes because rules cannot receive dependencies.
options.rationale: The rules method supports container injection, so its returned rules are applied.
options.misconception: The rules method supports container injection, so its returned rules are applied.
